Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts · Conversation, family & daily routines

telling the time phrase

also o’clock, time on the clock, five past, ten past, quarter past, twenty past, twenty-five past, half past, twenty-five to, twenty to, quarter to, ten to, five to, twelfths of the hour, a twelfth of an hour, five-minute steps

modern

Andresian p. 49: hōra nōna cum quadrante
M-O s.v. o’clock, after Egger: est hōra septima cum quadrante
Plin. NH 2.58: dōdrantēs sēmunciās hōrārum

1The twelfths are used of the hour in Pliny, as lengths of time rather than readings of a clock: the moon shines longer each day by dōdrantēs sēmunciās hōrārum (NH 2.58); the stars are not seen until a dōdrāns hōrae before sunrise (18.219); the moon gains a dēxtāns hōrae and a sīcīlicus a night (18.324). Elsewhere he gives fractions of the hour in the Greek way (bis quīnta pars, tertiae duae, 6.213–218), and once joins one to the hours with cum (6.214). Telling the clock time by the quarter-hour is modern Latin: Traupman 81 with et; Egger (quoted in M-O s.v. o’clock) and Andresian p. 49 with cum. Every twelfth, in steps of five minutes, is current spoken Latin (see the sources).

hōra prīma cum ūnciā1

five past one, and so on: the hour, then cum and the twelfths of the hour

Each twelfth of the hour (ūncia hōrae) is five minutes, and the hour takes them with cum and the ablative: :05 cum ūnciā · :10 cum sextante · :15 cum quadrante · :20 cum triente · :25 cum quīncūnce · :30 cum sēmisse · :35 cum septūnce · :40 cum besse · :45 cum dōdrante · :50 cum dēxtante · :55 cum deūnce. The hour is the ordinal (prīma … duodecima); “at” a time puts the hour in the ablative: hōrā octāvā cum sextante, at ten past eight.

Other words

  • hōra prīma et quadrāns — a quarter past one, with et

    also used · modern · Traupman 81

    Traupman gives the quarter-hours this way: prīma hōra et quadrāns, et sēmihōra, et dōdrāns; “at” hōrā septimā et quadrante.

  • hōra prīma minūta quīnta decima — 1:15, counted by the minute

    also used · modern · Traupman 81

Examples

  • Est hōra septima cum quadrante.

    It’s a quarter past seven.M-O s.v. o’clock, after Egger

  • Est prīma hōra et quadrāns.

    It’s a quarter past one.Traupman 81

  • Hōrā septimā et dōdrante.

    At a quarter to eight.Traupman 81

  • longissimus diēs est aequinoctiālium hōrārum XIIII atque dīmidiae cum trīcēsimā ūnius hōrae

    the longest day is fourteen and a half equinoctial hours, with a thirtieth of an hourPlin. NH 6.214

  • Hōrā sextā cum besse cēnābimus.

    We’ll have dinner at twenty to seven.composed
